title: The Girl Who Followed the Rain
subtitle: 随雨而行的女孩
intro: 海边山丘上的一段传说。
stanzas:
Upon a hill beside the sea,
Where silver waters gleam,
A little maiden wandered free,
As though within a dream.

Her hair was pale as winter light,
Her eyes of azure hue;
She walked beneath the falling night,
Where lonely wildflowers grew.

They said she laughed when thunder cried,
And danced when tempests came;
Yet none could tell what dreams she'd hide,
Or why she feared the flame.

One evening, when the stars were gone,
She heard a distant call;
And through the mist before the dawn,
She passed the garden wall.

The rain had washed the winding track,
The sea was dark and deep;
And though the winds called, “Turn you back,”
She had no wish to sleep.

At last she reached the cliff's high stone,
Where restless waters lay;
And there she stood, so still, alone,
Until the break of day.

But when the morning touched the shore,
No footprints marked the sand;
They searched the cliffs for evermore,
Yet found no trace of hand.

And still, when storms approach the bay,
The fishermen declare
A maiden walks the cliffs at day,
With silver in her hair.

She sings no song of grief or fear,
Nor asks the sea for rest;
But those who wander lost may hear
Her voice beyond the west.

And some believe she never fell,
Nor vanished in the foam;
She merely followed, none can tell,
A road that led her home.

title: The Lamp upon the Hill
subtitle: 山丘上的灯
intro: 雨停之后，一辆单车经过小镇。
stanzas:
The rain had ceased at half-past five;
The gutters murmured still.
She wheeled her cycle from the gate
And started down the hill.

Her coat was folded in the frame,
Her sleeves above her wrist;
The lamps along the lower road
Were yellow in the mist.

Below the bridge she found a boy
Who watched the water run;
He held a loaf beneath his shirt
And waited for someone.

“My sister said to meet her here;
She works beyond the square.”
He pointed where the evening wind
Had stripped the branches bare.

She set her cycle by the wall
And looked towards the town;
Then took her coat from out the frame
And wrapped him, bending down.

“Come, show me where your sister works.”
She let him lead the way;
Her wheels went clicking at their heels
Beside the narrow quay.

They found the shutters fastened tight,
The doorway dark and wet;
He stood upon the step a while.
“She has not finished yet.”

She knocked upon the side-door twice;
A bolt slid back within.
A woman, white with flour and fear,
Came out and drew him in.

The loaf had broken in his shirt;
He gathered every crumb.
His sister brushed his dripping hair
And could not speak for some.

She turned to thank the waiting girl,
But heard, beyond the square,
A little bell, a turning wheel—
And found no person there.

title: At the Ferry
subtitle: 渡口
intro: 清冷的渡口，一次短暂的相遇。
stanzas:
I met her by the ferry-side,
Beneath the willow bough;
Her silver hair fell past her cheek
As she bent to loose the prow.

The rope was stiff with last night’s cold;
The seats were dark with rain.
A yellow leaf beneath the boat
Was caught against the chain.

“She’s fast,” she said. “The water’s low.”
She laid the pole aside.
“Will you take hold?” We pushed her clear,
And held her at the side.

“You’ve crossed before?” I asked of her.
“Once. We were three that day.”
She gathered up the trailing rope
And put the coil away.

A moment, with her hand at rest,
She looked along the shore;
Then set her bundle by her feet
And reached to take the oar.

Her silver hair in loosened curls
Fell softly, with a sheen;
She drew it back beneath her coat
And watched the space between.

The boat swung slowly from the bank;
She thanked me, bending low
To fit the oar against its pin
And turn the narrow bow.

The willow stirred above my head;
Its branches brushed the stream.
She passed beneath their broken shade,
And through the morning gleam.

translation.title: 中文译文
stanzas:
我在渡口遇见她，
就在低垂的柳枝下；
银发从她脸颊旁垂落，
当她俯身解开船头的系绳。

昨夜的寒气使缆绳发僵，
座板被雨水浸得深暗；
小船下面，一片黄叶
卡在铁链旁边。

“搁住了，”她说，“水浅了。”
她把长篙放到一旁。
“能扶一把吗？”我们将船推离浅滩，
扶稳在岸边。

“你以前渡过这里？”我问。
“有一次。那天我们三个。”
她收起拖在水里的绳子，
把绳圈放好。

她的手停了一会儿，
目光沿着河岸移去；
随后把行囊放在脚边，
伸手取过船桨。

银发松松地卷着，
柔柔垂落，泛着微光；
她把头发拢回外套里，
望着船与岸之间渐开的水面。

小船慢慢转离河岸；
她道了谢，俯下身，
将船桨安进桨架，
调转窄窄的船头。

头顶的柳枝轻轻摇动，
梢头拂过流水；
她驶过枝影断续的地方，
进入清晨的微光。

title: 光
subtitle: The Prelude · Book XIV
intro: 《序曲》第十四卷 · 斯诺登山节选
author: William Wordsworth
stanzas:
When at my feet the ground appeared to brighten,
And with a step or two seemed brighter still;
Nor was time given to ask or learn the cause,
For instantly a light upon the turf
Fell like a flash, and lo! as I looked up,
The Moon hung naked in a firmament
Of azure without cloud, and at my feet
Rested a silent sea of hoary mist.

translation.title: 中文试译
stanzas:
脚下的地面仿佛渐渐亮了起来，
又走一两步，便觉得更加明亮；
还未来得及追问或弄清缘由，
一道光忽然落在草地上，
如闪电一掠；看啊，当我抬起头，
月亮无遮无掩，悬在
澄蓝无云的苍穹；而在我的脚下，
静卧着一片灰白的雾海。

source.note: William Wordsworth，《序曲》1850 年版，第十四卷，登临斯诺登山段落节选。

title: Wandern
subtitle: The Pass of Kirkstone
intro: 柯克斯通山隘 · 开篇节选
author: William Wordsworth
stanzas:
Within the mind strong fancies work,
A deep delight the bosom thrills,
Oft as I pass along the fork
Of these fraternal hills:
Where, save the rugged road, we find
No appanage of human kind,
Nor hint of man; if stone or rock
Seem not his handy-work to mock …

translation.title: 中文试译
stanzas:
心中，强烈的想象涌动，
深深的欣悦震颤着胸怀，
每当我穿行于
这相依群山的分岔之间：
在这里，除了一条崎岖的路，
找不到任何属于人世的事物，
也没有人的踪迹；除非那些山石
仿佛正在摹仿人手的造作……

source.note: 《柯克斯通山隘》开篇八行；结尾省略后文。

title: 古舟子咏
subtitle: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
intro: 风暴中的海洋，神秘而不可预测的力量。
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
stanzas:
The upper air burst into life!
And a hundred fire-flags sheen,
To and fro they were hurried about!
And to and fro, and in and out,
The wan stars danced between.
creationNote: 巨大的少女伫立于风暴中的海洋，裙摆向左扬起，水流沿布料滴落。借鉴诗歌的超自然海洋意象；画面人物并非原诗中的角色。

title: 潮起潮落
subtitle: The Tide Rises, the Tide Falls
intro: 无尽的潮汐，时间的循环与生命的有限。
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
stanzas:
The tide rises, the tide falls,
The twilight darkens, the curlew calls;
Along the sea-sands damp and brown
The traveller hastens toward the town,
    And the tide rises, the tide falls.

Darkness settles on roofs and walls,
But the sea, the sea in the darkness calls;
The little waves, with their soft, white hands,
Efface the footprints in the sands,
    And the tide rises, the tide falls.

The morning breaks; the steeds in their stalls
Stamp and neigh, as the hostler calls;
The day returns, but nevermore
Returns the traveller to the shore,
    And the tide rises, the tide falls.
creationNote: 纤细的少女独自站在海岸，面对汹涌海浪；通过人物与大海的尺度对比，呼应潮汐、消逝与时间。
